64169c8c9e3e95678dcd0fe8ef71a1bbd5298056.summary: Socket reports 13 malicious NuGet packages used in a campaign that lures .NET developers with fake take-home job assessments. Building or running a lure project triggers a build-time MSBuild stager and a runtime control that launches a DLL side-loading pair. Other packages download and run executables from GitHub. Related fake axios repositories carry loaders and a Chrome profile stealer, and a trojanized crypto wallet app was also used. The campaign is not attributed to a named threat actor.

hedges: We could not determine how the Home Assessment lures reach candidates; we found no recruiter message, email or job post for them.
We have not attributed this campaign to a named threat actor.
Take-home tests resemble lures that public reporting links to North Korea, but no shared indicator or code was found with published campaigns.
We did not test the side-load, and whether a copied osk.exe starts from the user's local app data folder on current Windows builds remains an open question.
Download counts include mirrors and scanners and are not victim counts.
We could not determine whether the repository belongs to the threat actor or to a targeted developer, so we do not name it.
The link between WinUI.Button and the rest of the cluster rests on naming and technique, not a shared indicator.
We treat that as timing evidence only.
